4.0.s.en: (1) The widow and the blessing of the oil

4.0.0.en: Creditor: one who lends to the needy and takes interest on it.

4.0.1.en: If Elijah concentrated his work on the wicked King Ahab and on proclaiming the truth about the worship of God, instead of Baal, before the people, Elisha did not care about King Joram and refused to deal with him and did not help him, except for the sake of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he concentrated his ministry on those who believed in God and the sons of the prophets, to solve their problems, especially the poverty from which they suffered.

4.0.2.en: One of the sons of the prophets died, a man who feared God, from the school of the prophets whom Elisha led after Elijah, and he was known to Elisha because he was their leader, and he was probably young. He left a widow and two sons, and his family was exposed to severe poverty. The widow began to take some gifts, but they did not suffice her, and she was forced to give up many of her possessions, even the necessary ones. Then she resorted to borrowing from the creditor, and the debts and their interest increased, and she found no means to repay what she owed. Here the creditor threatened to take her two sons as bondmen to himself, or to sell them, which the Law allows. So the widow resorted to Elisha, as the leader of the prophets, the man of God, and the father who feels for his children. Although Elisha was a celibate, he bore a fatherhood toward all his people, especially the prophets who serve God and their families, and even more toward this family and the like of it, who had lost their chief provider.

4.1.0.en: Elisha cared about this widow and did not try to come to an understanding with the creditor, because he might be greedy and hard-hearted; so he took care to examine the widow's possessions and discovered her great poverty, to the point that she had nothing of furniture or food except a pot of oil in one of the vessels, enough only to anoint a piece of bread.

4.2.0.en: Elisha believed in the power of God, who is able to do all things, so he was not troubled by the great poverty from which this widow suffered, but in confidence asked her to borrow empty vessels from her neighbors and to borrow as many as she could. This borrowing shows the following:

4.2.1.en: 1- God cares about man's striving and his readiness to receive the grace of God.

4.2.2.en: 2- According to the widow's faith she would gather many vessels, to be filled, all of them, with the blessing of God.

4.2.3.en: 3- The cooperation of her neighbors helps in working the miracle.

4.2.4.en: 4- The grace of God is given with a generosity that surpasses reason.

4.2.5.en: 5- Elisha did not care to postpone the creditor's demand, or to give him part of the money, but wanted to enrich the widow so that she would pay what she owed and have a surplus, that she might live honored and loved by God, with her needs met and her husband, who feared God, honored.

4.3.0.en: Elisha commanded the widow, after gathering the many vessels, to shut the door of her house upon herself, so that she and her two sons would be alone, for the following reasons:

4.3.1.en: 1- Elisha did not go with her, so that she would trust that the miracle was from the hand of God and not Elisha's personal power. This shows Elisha's humility and his glorifying of God.

4.3.2.en: 2- Only those who believe in the miracle would enjoy seeing it, that is, the widow and her two sons, who were at a high level of faith, and their need made them cling to God, since they had probably learned the fear of God from the provider of the family who had departed.

4.3.3.en: 3- It shows the faith of Elisha, who commanded her to pour out the oil, then lifted up a prayer for God to complete the miracle, for he was confident of God's fatherhood, His love and His power.

4.3.4.en: 4- Elisha's command to pour out the oil shows the widow's faith in obeying his command, so she received the blessing of the miracle, for she had nothing but a pot of oil, and she believed that the vessels would be filled, and she set aside one vessel after another as it was filled.

4.3.5.en: 5- Perhaps the neighbors, if they saw the miracle, would covet this oil and take from her, relying on the fact that the vessels were their vessels and that they had some right to this oil; but the miracle depends on the widow's faith.

4.3.6.en: 6- Shutting the door signifies the importance of man's inner life, such as prayer, fasting and reading the Holy Bible ... and all private spiritual striving.

4.4.0.en: The woman obeyed all that Elisha commanded her. She gathered as many vessels as possible and went into her house and shut the door upon herself and her two sons, and perhaps she stood praying with her sons, while they brought her one vessel after another, and she poured oil into it.

4.4.1.en: She saw with her own eyes the wonderful miracle, how the pot of oil became a continuous spring of oil, flowing to fill one vessel after another, and of course her heart and her sons' hearts were lifted up in praise and thanksgiving to God.

4.5.0.en: All the vessels were filled, and she asked her sons whether there was still an empty vessel, to bring it to her. They answered that all the vessels were full and there was not one empty vessel left. Then the flow of the oil stopped.

4.5.1.en: The grace of God is very generous and ready to give you all that you need, according to your care to come to God, and He fills you with His grace; and according to your readiness to give, God gives you largeness of heart and strength, so you give generously and rejoice and make everyone around you rejoice.

4.6.0.en: The widow returned to tell Elisha what had happened, and he told her to go and sell the oil that had gathered in the vessels she had, and pay the debt with the price of what she sold of it, and live on the remainder, she and her two sons. We note that the woman took care to return to Elisha and ask him what to do after the miracle had happened, and this means two things:

4.6.1.en: 1- We ought to return with thanksgiving to God after every grace He gives us.

4.6.2.en: 2- We ought to ask Him in the matters of our life, even if they are clear matters. She now had oil to sell and with which to pay her debts, but her submission to God made her return and ask the man of God. Your asking your father of confession and spiritual guide is a return to God to hear His voice, not out of doubt about what you are doing but out of readiness for a constant hearing of the voice of God, even if He commands you the opposite of what you expected.

4.6.3.en: You are indebted to God and to His children with all your life, because Christ bought you and paid your price when you had been sentenced to death. So take care to pay your debts by offering love to everyone, and offer love to others before you care for your personal needs. The woman paid her debts before spending on her living. Be confident that God's goodness is abundant and will guarantee all your needs, even if matters become critical and reach distress or severe poverty, for God is ready to work miracles in every generation.

4.7.0.en: Shunem: a city opposite Mount Gilboa, called today "Solem," in the land of the tribe of Issachar, about six kilometers east of Jezreel and twenty-five kilometers from Mount Carmel, where the Shunammite woman went to look for Elisha.

4.7.1.en: Elisha traveled much, to visit his people and the schools of the prophets, and Shunem was in a middle place between many regions, such as Carmel, the plain of Jezreel, Nazareth and Galilee, so he passed through it often. In this city there was a woman who was rich and of a known standing in the city, and she invited him to her house to eat bread, and this hospitality was repeated whenever Elisha passed by Shunem. This shows:

4.7.2.en: 1- The virtue of generosity and hospitality to strangers, for which this woman was distinguished.

4.7.3.en: 2- This woman's care and faith in the blessing of the man of God, for her greatness and their wealth did not distract her from receiving the blessing of God, and this was not a kind of pride or show, as the coming verses show her humility and quietness.

4.7.4.en: Your offering love to every needy person, or to one passing through special circumstances, opens many doors for you to receive God's blessing in your life, and even gives you things you did not ask for, for God cannot be in debt to anyone. If you give something to His children, He gives you manifold more.

4.8.2.en: The woman sensed the holiness and righteousness of the man of God through his brief visits to her house, and longed to receive a greater blessing from him. So she said to her husband that Elisha passed by them often, and suggested to him that they prepare for him a little chamber on the roof of the house and put in it a bed and a table and a stool and a lamp, so that when he visited them on one of his journeys he might rest and sleep in the chamber.

4.8.3.en: This shows that the woman saw in Elisha's conduct a spiritual way of life and not only that he was a prophet, so she wanted to learn and be a disciple at his hands, and at the same time she took care to prepare for him his necessary needs, so that he might rest amid the toils of travel, by preparing a place in which the needs of rest are provided, namely a bed, and a table on which to eat or to read, and a lamp to help him read. She did not care to show her wealth as a display of greatness before people, but to provide for the needs of this great servant.

4.8.4.en: Elisha must have found his rest in this house; therefore he passed by it repeatedly, as Christ was accustomed to pass by the house of Lazarus in Bethany. This means that this woman and her house were marked by spiritual qualities in which the man of God found rest. Here we see God's care in providing for the needs of His servants and their rest; if Elisha cared about visiting his people, God provides everything that gives him rest materially and not only spiritually.

4.9.s.en: (3) The promise of a son to the Shunammite

4.9.0.en: On one of Elisha's journeys he passed through the city of Shunem and entered the house of the great woman to rest there, and after he slept in his upper chamber in her house, he asked Gehazi his disciple to call the woman and convey to her his great appreciation for her toil for him and his disciple, in hosting them and her care in building the chamber and furnishing it and everything connected with their hospitality, and to make clear to her Elisha's readiness to repay her kindness by solving any problem she met, which needed intercession with the king or the captain of the host. Although Elisha kept apart from Jehoram king of Israel because of his evils and idol worship, in love he was ready to go to the king and speak to him about this woman's requests, and the king respected and feared Elisha because of his connection with God. This shows Elisha's appreciation of the services done to him and his wish to return the love, to serve her in any need she might have. Although this woman was great and had possessions and of course had some problems, as most rich people meet, she asked nothing of Elisha and said that she dwelt among her own people, though her people, the kingdom of Israel, were Jews among whom the worship of idols had entered; but she focused on the fact that they were the people of God who believe in Him, and therefore she lived in security through this faith. This shows the extent of her faith and her reliance on God. Wealth drives many to love of money and greed, but this woman stood firm in her faith and thanksgiving to God, and so was an example for the godly rich. Besides, as a human being she must have had needs, as will appear in the following verses: she was deprived of children, but her great reliance made her not ask even for this necessary thing.

4.9.1.en: Elisha's carefulness appears in that the woman did not enter his private chamber, but only his disciple Gehazi, because it was like the monk's cell. The woman's courtesy also appears, despite her greatness, and her respect for the man of God, although his chamber was part of her house.

4.9.2.en: How beautiful it is to be content with the grace of God that is with you, and to thank Him for everything and enjoy His care and richness, so that He gives you what you need without your asking, and you touch the hand of God and His fatherhood and tenderness.

4.10.0.en: After the woman went away, Elisha's heart remained occupied with repaying her kindness, and he began to consider with Gehazi his disciple what to do for her. This shows Elisha's humility in taking his disciple's counsel. With familiarity Gehazi said that he had noticed that she had no children, and the woman was not young, and in addition her husband was much older than she and had become old. So Elisha accepted his disciple's drawing his attention to this need.

4.11.0.en: According to the time of life: the period of pregnancy, that is, nine months.

4.11.1.en: Elisha responded at once to his disciple's reminder, for he had found the way to honor the woman. So he called her, and she stood reverently at the door of his chamber and did not enter, and he gave her the good news that after nine months God would give her a son. This news was a surprise beyond the woman's reason, and she did not believe it, so that she said to Elisha: Do not lie unto thine handmaid. She did not mean to accuse the man of God of lying, but she was expressing the difficulty of believing this joyful news, because human logic makes this matter almost impossible.

4.11.2.en: The woman's words show her great humility, for she said to him "my lord" and described herself as his handmaid. She did not use her reason in pride in not believing the news, because she was very humble, but the matter indeed surpasses human reason.

4.11.3.en: I wish you would trust the love of God, who wants to give you many blessings that surpass reason. The multitude of your sins does not hinder the work of God as long as you are pressing on in the way of repentance; rather, the grace of God abounds with the weak.

4.12.0.en: The woman's doubts began to recede and she took in the joyful miraculous news, then the news was confirmed by her conceiving, and she was in great joy beyond expression, and the joy was completed by her bearing a son.

4.13.s.en: (4) The raising of the Shunammite's son

4.13.0.en: The years passed and the child grew. One day he went with his father to the fields they owned, to oversee the reapers as they gathered the harvest. The city of Shunem had fertile lands. The Shunammite woman's husband was rich and owned many fields, and he went out to oversee the reaping himself. The gathering of the harvest is the most important stage in farming, because from it he gets the toil of the whole year, and sells it.

4.14.0.en: Suddenly the boy felt a severe pain in his head which made him cry out, "My head, my head." His father commanded one of his workers to carry him to his house, to his mother. It was a severe sunstroke which the little boy could not bear, and his father felt the seriousness of the situation, so he did not wait until the end of the day but carried him quickly to his house to rest. It seems that because everyone was busy with the harvest they did not care to keep the boy out of the rays of the sun, whose heat he could not bear.

4.15.0.en: The servant brought him to his mother, and she held him on her knees all the morning, until noon came and the boy died. The mother in her tenderness was trying to calm the child, not knowing what to do for him, while the dryness inside him increased until he lost consciousness and then departed from life.

4.16.0.en: Despite the horror of the sudden event, the woman's faith was not shaken, so she carried her dead son and went up with him to the chamber that she had prepared for Elisha and laid him on the bed of the man of God. Perhaps she remembered Elijah the prophet's raising of the son of the widow of Zarephath of Sidon from death (1 Kgs 17:17-21), and believed that Elisha, who had given her this son from God, was able also to raise him from the dead. As her barren womb, unable to bear, that is, dead to conceiving and bearing, God had brought this life out of, so He is able also to bring out of death new life for her son. Perhaps she remembered her mother Sarah, the wife of our father Abraham, and how God brought out of the deadness of her womb a new life, namely Isaac, for God is able at all times to give life out of death. Perhaps she resembled our father Abraham, who believed, when he went forward to sacrifice Isaac, that God was able to raise him from the dead.

4.16.1.en: Perhaps her faith that God was able to raise her son made her hold herself together and not weep, so she rose above the feelings of motherhood which could tear her heart, and was at peace and trusted God, who would not leave her.

4.17.1.en: In faith the woman sent to her husband, telling him that she would go to the man of God at Carmel, where he dwelt. She asked her husband for one of his workers and a donkey, to take her there. Her husband wondered and asked her why she was going, since it was not the day of a religious celebration, which was what he used to do on the sabbath or the new moon. It seems that Carmel, where Elijah had built an altar and the fire consumed his sacrifice and he killed the prophets of Baal (1 Kgs 18:30), had become a holy place where Elisha held religious celebrations and sacrifices.

4.17.2.en: It is remarkable that in complete faith the woman answered her husband and reassured him that all was well and peaceful, and that it was a visit to be blessed by the man of God. This shows the extent of the woman's faith and her peace that surpasses reason, which is a divine grace that God gave her because of her faith.

4.17.3.en: If you remember the God who is with you and His power that supports you, you will not be troubled by any problem or distress, confident that God by your prayers will intervene and rescue you from it; indeed, from the steadiness of your peace you can reassure those around you.

4.18.0.en: The woman rode on the donkey and commanded the servant to drive the donkey fast, without fearing to cause her fatigue, unless she herself asked him to slow down. This shows the feelings of motherhood that moved her in longing for the raising of her son, so that she might rejoice in him.

4.19.0.en: She set out on her journey until she reached Elisha, who was then on Mount Carmel.

4.19.1.en: Elisha saw her coming while she was still a long way from him, and recognized her, and told his servant that it was the Shunammite woman coming toward them.

4.20.0.en: He asked his servant to run to meet her and to inquire about her welfare and that of her husband and her son, and she said to him, It is well. Here the heart of Elisha, full of love, appears, and how he sensed the woman's need from her hastening toward him, so he quickly sent to her his disciple Gehazi to ask about her welfare and that of those with her. It is remarkable that in strong faith she said, It is well, for she was confident that Elisha would raise her son.

4.21.0.en: The Shunammite woman reached Elisha, who was staying on Mount Carmel, and she got down from the donkey and hurried to him and bowed down and caught him by the feet, in a clinging that proclaims how much she needed the prophet. Elisha felt the bitterness of her heart and her pains and had compassion on her. But his disciple Gehazi felt that catching Elisha by the feet was lacking in respect for him and tried to push her away from Elisha, but the man of God stopped him, by his sense of her troubles. Gehazi, because of the hardness of his heart, did not feel the woman's pains and condemned her because she did not respect the man of God, but Elisha, the man of prayer, felt for her and had compassion on her.

4.21.1.en: God hid the boy's illness from Elisha, so that he would not go to him and heal him and it would become an ordinary healing miracle, and He allowed him to die so that the power of God would appear, by the hand of Elisha, in raising him, and God would be glorified; and at the same time it was a showing of the extent of this woman's faith, so she deserved this great miracle, which will appear after some verses.

4.21.2.en: From this it appears that the revealing of the unseen to the prophets and the gifted men of God is only to the extent that God allows and not in all things, for God lets them know some matters to help them in ministry and for the glorifying of His holy name.

4.22.0.en: With bitterness of heart the woman told Elisha that she had not asked for a son, and when he gave her the good news of bearing a son she had said to him: "Why do you lie to me and deceive me?" since she saw herself unworthy of this son. Elisha understood that her son had died and that she would have preferred to have no son rather than to bear a son and become emotionally attached to him and then have him die. Her saying, Did I not say, Do not deceive me, does not mean that Elisha deceived her, but means her confidence that Elisha had not deceived her and consequently would raise her son, because God, who spoke by the mouth of Elisha, cannot lie. Although she did not prefer to have a son who would die, at the same time she trusted that God was able to raise him.

4.23.0.en: As the Lord liveth, and as thy soul liveth: an oath by the life of God and of Elisha.

4.23.1.en: Gird up thy loins: that is, to put on the clothes that are worn about the waist down to the thighs, and what is meant is readiness for the journey.

4.23.2.en: Elisha commanded his disciple Gehazi to prepare for the journey, to go to Shunem to the woman's house, and not to be occupied on the way with blessing anyone in need of a blessing, or accepting good words and blessing from others, that is, not to be occupied with anything on the way, even other services, in order to hasten to reach the dead boy. He asked him to carry Elisha's staff to lay it upon the face of the dead boy, that he might rise. Elisha forgot that the power is not in the staff but in the prayer he lifts up, as he thought in the past when he took Elijah's mantle and tried to divide the Jordan River, and it did not divide until he prayed and asked for the power of God that was with Elijah, and then he divided the river.

4.23.3.en: The woman did not accept Gehazi's being sent, but clung to Elisha and declared with an oath that she would not leave him. The woman understood the right course and drew Elisha's attention to it by her clinging to him, so he arose with her to go to her house; for since she was confident that Elisha was the source of the blessing, she insisted that he come with her.

4.23.4.en: We note that the woman's oath, "As the Lord liveth, and as thy soul liveth," is the same oath that Elisha said to Elijah when he tried to part from him, before Elijah's ascent. So God reminds him of Elijah's faith and the power of God working in him, so that he might rise with the woman and pray for the dead boy.

4.24.0.en: Gehazi carried out the word of his master Elisha and hastened ahead of him to the woman's house, to lay Elisha's staff on the boy's face, but there was neither voice nor hearing, and he remained dead, so he returned and told Elisha of the uselessness of what he had done. This is a confirmation of the necessity of the coming of Elisha, the man of God, to pray for the boy. Gehazi's obedience is blessed because it confirmed to Elisha the necessity of prayer and that he should serve in person and care for this boy.

4.25.0.en: Elisha reached the woman's house and went up to his chamber and found the boy lying on his bed, so he shut the door of the chamber upon himself and the dead boy, that he might pray to God in quiet. Shutting the door in prayer means casting away the thoughts and preoccupations of the world and concentrating on speaking with God, the only source of power for our life.

4.25.1.en: God rejoices in your prayer, especially if you give yourself wholly to Him, rejecting all the preoccupations of the world and all reliance on human power, and so you experience the power of God and His care for you. And when you shut the door of your closet, shut also the door of your senses and thoughts, so that you may be wholly with God.

4.26.0.en: Elisha was not content with praying beside the dead boy's bed, but lay upon the child and stretched himself upon him, and put his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands, and continued his prayers. That is, Elisha completed his striving, asking for the power of God, and the power of prayer worked and its warmth passed from Elisha's body to the body of the dead boy, so that warmth went through it, that is, life began to stir in him, but he remained in a coma and did not move. We note that God did not work the miracle quickly, so that Elisha might offer continuous striving in prayer with steadfast faith, and so his faith would be strengthened and he would see with his own eyes the greatness of the miracle when it is accomplished in stages.

4.26.1.en: God allowed Elisha to use material means, namely his lying upon the boy, as He used in his earlier miracles salt and meal ... and as the Church now uses materials in her most important works, namely the holy sacraments, so that man may offer what he has and touch with his hands the material part of the miracle, and not doubt, but by his faith perceive the power of God that works the miracle. Striving is necessary for receiving grace, which does everything and works the miracles.

4.26.2.en: Perhaps Elisha's lying upon the boy and putting his mouth upon his mouth was meant to transfer life from himself to the dead body, as Christ united with us in His Incarnation, and taking our mortal body gave us His life and raised us in Him, that we may live forever with Him, as we say in the Friday praise, "He took what is ours and gave us what is His," that is, He bore our death for us and gave us His life.

4.27.0.en: After Elisha's prayers and his stretching himself upon the dead boy until his body grew warm, he arose to continue the prayer, having been encouraged and his faith strengthened when the boy's body grew warm. He walked to and fro in the house, standing in more than one place inside the house, continuing the prayer with insistence for God to intervene. And after he felt peace in his heart, he stretched himself upon the boy again, and the miracle was accomplished, in that the boy sneezed seven times, then opened his eyes, declaring that he had returned to life.

4.27.1.en: The miracle was accomplished for the following reasons:

4.27.2.en: 1- The faith of Elisha the prophet, which appeared in his many prayers.

4.27.3.en: 2- Elisha's love for his children and his people, that is, this woman, and his going with her to her house to pray over the dead.

4.27.4.en: 3- Elisha's striving and perseverance and his lying twice upon the boy.

4.27.5.en: 4- The woman's faith and her clinging to Elisha, that he might come and pray for the boy.

4.28.0.en: Elisha opened the door of the chamber, where Gehazi was standing watching the situation, and commanded him to call the boy's mother, who came in haste. He called her to enter, and when she entered he said to her, Take up thy son.

4.28.1.en: We see in this verse that Elisha called the woman three times, in (vv. 12, 15, 36). The first time her reliance on God appeared, the second time she received the joyful news of the birth of the child, and the third time she received the raising of her only son. She signifies the soul that believes in God and obeys His call, for if it relies on Him it receives joy in its life and the experience of resurrection with Christ in all its conduct.

4.29.0.en: When the woman learned from Gehazi of the raising of her son, she hastened to Elisha to bow down before him, offering her deep thanks and her submission to God in the person of Elisha, and her readiness to hold fast to the commandments of God and His teachings, which the man of God proclaims. After this she went to her son, lying on the bed, to embrace him and rejoice in him.

4.29.1.en: Take care to offer thanks to God before you are occupied with His gifts, for God is the giver of these gifts; how then can you be occupied with them rather than with Him! And thank also the saints who have helped you and every person who has done you a service.

4.30.s.en: (5) The healing of the poisoned food

4.30.0.en: After the raising of the Shunammite's son, Elisha left Shunem and did not return to Carmel, but went east to Gilgal, beside the Jordan River, to visit the sons of the prophets. It is clear from Elisha's life that he cared about visiting his children, strengthening their faith, tending them and providing for their needs. He gathered with the sons of the prophets and they sat before him, as he taught them his life-giving teachings. After this he had to care for their material food, as Christ taught the multitudes and also took care to feed them with the two fishes and the five loaves. But there was a dearth in the land for some time, that is, they had no food, and Elisha, the man of faith, was not troubled, but asked his disciple Gehazi to bring the great pot in which they prepared food, though there was no food, for he was confident that God would feed His children. He asked Gehazi to bring any kind of plants and boil them to feed the men.

4.31.0.en: Wild gourds: the wild cucumber, and it is probably the colocynth, whose taste is bitter and which causes violent diarrhea, colic and vomiting.

4.31.1.en: It seems that Gehazi did not hasten to bring something to boil, as Elisha had commanded him. One of the sons of the prophets was commissioned to gather herbs from the field. But it seems that he found none, because of the famine, but he found wild gourds, and thought them fit for eating, so he gathered a quantity in his lap and brought it to the house and cut it up and put it into the pot.

4.31.2.en: Here the lack of care and the danger of negligence appear, into which Gehazi fell, and likewise one of the prophets who gathered harmful food. So be careful in your words and actions, lest you harm those around you and wrong them without intending to, and so trouble and distress them. Be obedient to your spiritual fathers, quick to carry out their words; then God will support you and guide you and protect you from many troubles.

4.32.0.en: After the gourds were boiled, the men began to eat, and they felt the bitterness of the food and expected death because of this poisonous food, so they cried out to Elisha their leader to rescue them.

4.32.1.en: Perhaps God allowed the famine, and then also allowed the presence of these poisonous plants, to warn His people Israel, who had mixed their worship with the worship of idols, so that they might take heed through these distresses and put away their evils to live with Him. Sin causes death and prevents blessings; on the contrary, when the children of God are present, blessings spread and they rescue others from destruction, as will happen at the hand of Elisha.

4.33.0.en: Elisha commanded that the poisonous food be gathered and put again into the pot, then commanded them to bring a little meal, and blessed it, then cast it into the pot, and in faith in the love of God and His care he asked them to pour out for the men in their dishes, confident that God had removed the poison from this food. The men came forward in faith also to eat, trusting Elisha's command, and they ate and found it good, delicious food, and found it completely different from the first food. The meal signifies the Body of Christ, as the offering of the grain offering anciently in the days of Moses signified it. So also the bread that is changed into the Body of Christ in the Divine Liturgy, for Christ is able to save us from death and to put away from us all the evils of the devil.

4.33.1.en: When sin enters our daily life it becomes death for us, as it enters into smoking, wine and drugs, and into cheating in dealings between people, and into every evil thought that accompanies our works and words, so that death goes through us within, and there is no way of escape from it except prayer and repentance. When we return to God He rescues us from our evil deeds.

4.33.2.en: Believe in God in all your circumstances, however difficult they may seem, and He will turn evil into good and put away from you everything harmful, and you will live in assurance.

4.34.s.en: (6) The blessing of the twenty loaves

4.34.0.en: Baal-shalisha: a city that was perhaps near Gilgal.

4.34.1.en: Bread of the firstfruits: God commanded the offering of the firstfruits of the cultivated plants to Him (Lev 23:14). Full ears of corn: parched grain, which is wheat that has not completely ripened.

4.34.2.en: Husk (sack): a bag of cloth in which a man carries his belongings.

4.34.3.en: The famine was still general in the land, but God does not forget His children. A man who cared about carrying out the Law came to Elisha to offer the firstfruits of his farming, and gave the man of God twenty loaves and some parched grain for his own food. But Elisha did not care for himself but for his children, so he gave this gift to his children gathered around him, despite their great number, for he believed in the blessing of God. And as Christ blessed the two fishes and the five loaves, so also Elisha, who is a type of Christ, blessed the twenty loaves, and they fed the whole multitude.

4.35.0.en: Gehazi wondered at his master's words, for he saw that twenty loaves would of course not suffice a hundred men, just as the disciples wondered when they found only two fishes and five loaves and said, what are they among so many? (Jn 6:9). It is human weakness, for they did not look to the power of God. But the beautiful thing is that Gehazi obeyed his master, though not convinced, and when he distributed the food Elisha's word was fulfilled, for the loaves satisfied all and some was left over, as food was left over when Christ fed the multitudes. We note God's tenderness, for He worked the miracle despite Gehazi's weak faith; God is longsuffering and does not withhold His blessings, until our faith is perfected as long as we are obedient to His commands.

4.35.1.en: Obey the commandments of God, even if they surpass your understanding, confident that God will not leave you and will provide all your needs and protect you, and will even glorify you amid the hardest circumstances, because He is your Father and He loves you.
